title: A species that has gone extinct never reappears

fields.label: Label
fields.value: A species that has gone extinct never reappears

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Once a species has disappeared from the earth, the identical form never reappears, because any replacement would inherit different characters from its different progenitors.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. X: On the Geological Succession of Organic Beings

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: When a species has once disappeared from the face of the earth, we have reason to believe that the same identical form never reappears.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter X, “On the Geological Succession of Organic Beings”; section “Species once lost do not reappear”. Scope: all species in the fossil record

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch10-04: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.81

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The universal prediction is clear and searchable in a large public record. Confirming non-reappearance is asymmetric and taxonomic identity is imperfect, but counterexamples can decisively refute it.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Search dated occurrence records for species with a substantial global absence followed by later occurrences, then audit taxonomy and dating. A validated reappearance of the identical biological species would refute the claim; no such cases supports it only within detection limits.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Morphospecies identity may not equal biological-species identity.

Lazarus taxa usually reflect sampling gaps rather than true global extinction.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.9
data adequacy: 0.69
data existence: 0.93
operationalizability: 0.91
discriminating power: 0.6

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Stratigraphic ranges are public and can be screened for reappearances in weeks. Most gaps are sampling artefacts, so an apparent return rarely forces a true re-origin of the same species. The analysis can clear many Lazarus cases and still cannot certify that an identical form has never arisen twice.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Inspect species ranges for a disappearance followed by a later occurrence of the same species after a gap too long to be one continuous population. A later population that must be a new origin of the identical form would refute the claim; gaps explained by sampling would leave it standing.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Identical form is unstable where fossils are feature-poor and species names are applied inconsistently.

Incomplete sampling creates gaps that look like disappearance and return.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.8
analysis feasibility: 0.65
operationalizability: 0.6
discriminating power: 0.4
data adequacy: 0.5
